natural: keep one's tools hidden until the time comes

meaning.en: To keep one's talents in reserve and wait patiently for the right opportunity.
meaning.zh: 把才能藏在身上，等待合适的时机再施展。

examples.zh: 他藏器待时，三年后才推出新产品。
examples.en: He bided his time and launched the new product three years later.

examples.zh: 年轻人要藏器待时，不要急于表现。
examples.en: Young people should keep their talents in reserve rather than rush to show off.

story.en: The Book of Changes says: 'The gentleman keeps his tool about his person and acts when the time is right' (君子藏器于身，待时而动).
story.zh: 《周易·系辞下》：“君子藏器于身，待时而动，何不利之有？”

date.zh: 战国 · 约前4—前3世纪（《易传》）
date.en: Warring States, c. 4th–3rd c. BC (Yi Zhuan commentaries)

usage.en: Positive; stresses patience and modesty rather than lack of ability.
usage.zh: 褒义，强调耐心与谦逊，而非无能。

meaning.en: A very plain dwelling; a symbol of the frugal life of ancient sage-kings.
meaning.zh: 茅草屋顶，泥土台阶，形容房屋简陋，也指古代贤君的俭朴。

examples.zh: 相传尧帝居茅茨土阶，却天下大治。
examples.en: Legend says Emperor Yao lived in a thatched hut yet ruled well.

examples.zh: 山中老屋茅茨土阶，却别有风味。
examples.en: The old mountain house, thatched and earthen, has a charm of its own.

story.en: Sima Qian describes Yao and Shun: 'Their halls were three steps of earth, with thatch left untrimmed' (堂高三尺，土阶三等，茅茨不翦).
story.zh: 《史记·太史公自序》：“尧舜……堂高三尺，土阶三等，茅茨不翦，采椽不刮。”

usage.en: Literary; often praises frugality in rulers or the humble charm of a plain house.
usage.zh: 书面语，多赞颂君王俭朴或朴素的居所。

natural: nothing to worry about behind you

meaning.en: To have no worries about matters left at home or behind, and so be free to act.
meaning.zh: 不用担心后方或家里的事，可以放手去做。

equivalents: have no worries at one's back

examples.zh: 有家人支持，他出国创业后顾无忧。
examples.en: With his family behind him, he went abroad to start a business with no worries.

examples.zh: 公司完善的保障让员工后顾无忧。
examples.en: The company's good benefits leave employees with nothing to worry about.

usage.en: Often with 使/让…; typical of insurance, welfare and family-support contexts.
usage.zh: 常与“使、让”连用，多见于保障、家庭支持的语境。

natural: peach and plum trees filling the gate

meaning.en: To have students everywhere; a teacher with many outstanding pupils.
meaning.zh: 学生众多，遍及各处，多用来称赞教师。

equivalents: a teacher with a full house of pupils

examples.zh: 王教授执教四十年，桃李盈门。
examples.en: Professor Wang taught for forty years and his students are everywhere.

examples.zh: 祝老师桃李盈门，万事如意。
examples.en: May you, teacher, have students everywhere and every success.

usage.en: A compliment to teachers; also used in greetings on Teachers' Day.
usage.zh: 称赞教师，也用于教师节的祝词。

meaning.en: Any ordinary people at all; four of the commonest Chinese surnames used to mean 'everyone'.
meaning.zh: 泛指普通人，用最常见的几个姓表示“随便什么人”。

examples.zh: 这种事，不是张王李赵谁都能做的。
examples.en: This is not something any Tom, Dick or Harry can do.

examples.zh: 名单上全是张王李赵，没有一个知名人物。
examples.en: The list is all ordinary names, with no well-known figure.

usage.en: Informal; refers to unnamed ordinary people.
usage.zh: 口语，泛指不具名的普通人。

meaning.en: To speak in a vague, roundabout way so as not to say things plainly.
meaning.zh: 话说得含糊曲折，不肯明说。

examples.zh: 他对责任问题隐约其辞，不肯正面回答。
examples.en: He spoke in veiled terms about responsibility and refused a direct answer.

examples.zh: 文章隐约其辞，读者很难看出真意。
examples.en: The article is so vague that readers can hardly see its real point.

usage.en: Predicate; often implies deliberate evasion.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常含有意回避的意味。

natural: red in the face with a thick neck

meaning.en: Flushed with anger or excitement, as in a heated argument.
meaning.zh: 因生气或激动而脸红、脖子涨粗，形容争吵时的样子。

examples.zh: 他们为一点小事争得脸红脖子粗。
examples.en: They argued until they were red in the face over something trivial.

examples.zh: 有话好好说，别脸红脖子粗的。
examples.en: Talk calmly; no need to get red in the face.

usage.en: Colloquial; often follows 争得 or 吵得.
usage.zh: 口语，常接在“争得、吵得”之后。

meaning.en: Naughty and mischievous, especially of children.
meaning.zh: 顽皮淘气，爱闹事，多指孩子。

examples.zh: 这孩子从小就调皮捣蛋，没一刻安静。
examples.en: The child has been naughty since he was small, never still for a moment.

examples.zh: 班上有几个调皮捣蛋的男生。
examples.en: There are a few mischievous boys in the class.

usage.en: Casual and often affectionate; mostly about children.
usage.zh: 口语，常含喜爱之意，多指孩子。

natural: a grand pardon throughout the realm

meaning.en: An amnesty granted by a ruler throughout the realm, usually on a great occasion.
meaning.zh: 君主在重大时刻赦免天下罪犯。

examples.zh: 新帝登基，下诏大赦天下。
examples.en: The new emperor took the throne and decreed a general amnesty.

examples.zh: 戏里皇上一高兴就大赦天下。
examples.en: In the drama the emperor grants a general pardon whenever he is pleased.

usage.en: Historical; also used jokingly for relief from some obligation.
usage.zh: 多用于历史语境，也可戏谑地指被免除责任。

natural: turn one's face and show no feeling

meaning.en: To turn on someone abruptly, with no regard for old ties.
meaning.zh: 说翻脸就翻脸，毫不顾念旧情。

equivalents: drop one's friends without a second thought

examples.zh: 他得势之后，对老朋友翻脸无情。
examples.en: Once in power, he turned on his old friends without mercy.

examples.zh: 你怎么能这样翻脸无情？
examples.en: How can you turn on me so coldly?

usage.en: Predicate; strong criticism.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，批评意味较强。

natural: good fortune and joy to spare

meaning.en: A New Year wish for abundant good fortune and celebration.
meaning.zh: 祝愿吉祥喜庆，福气绰绰有余，多用于新春祝福。

equivalents: may joy and plenty be yours

examples.zh: 春联上写着“吉庆有余”。
examples.en: The Spring Festival couplet reads 'joy and plenty'.

examples.zh: 祝您新年吉庆有余，阖家安康！
examples.en: Wishing you joy and plenty in the new year, and health to your whole family!

usage.en: Auspicious wish; 余 puns with 鱼 (fish) in New Year imagery.
usage.zh: 吉祥话，“余”与“鱼”谐音，常见于年画。

meaning.en: Lingering affection for a former lover or a past relationship.
meaning.zh: 旧日的感情还没有完全断绝。

examples.zh: 分手多年，他对她仍余情未了。
examples.en: Years after the break-up he still carries a torch for her.

examples.zh: 两人见面时，余情未了。
examples.en: When they met, old feelings still lingered.

usage.en: Usually about love; can also mean leftover emotion after an event.
usage.zh: 多指爱情，也可指事后余留的情绪。

meaning.en: Utterly enchanting or overwhelming, leaving one entranced.
meaning.zh: 使人心神迷醉、魂魄震荡，形容极其动人或迷人。

examples.zh: 那首曲子销魂荡魄，听者无不动容。
examples.en: The tune was soul-stirring, and every listener was moved.

examples.zh: 她回眸一笑，销魂荡魄。
examples.en: Her backward glance and smile were enchanting.

usage.en: Literary; usually about beauty, music or passion. Not neutral in older fiction, where it can be risqué.
usage.zh: 书面语，多形容美色、音乐或情感；旧小说中有时带艳情意味。

meaning.en: Someone entirely at another's mercy, like meat waiting to be cut up.
meaning.zh: 砧板上的肉，比喻任人宰割、处境危险的人。

examples.zh: 落入敌手，他便成了俎上之肉。
examples.en: Once in enemy hands, he was meat on the block.

examples.zh: 小企业在巨头面前如俎上之肉。
examples.en: Small firms are at the mercy of the giants.

usage.en: Literary; 砧上鱼肉 is the same idea in another form.
usage.zh: 书面语；“砧上鱼肉”意思相同。

meaning.en: To hold the initiative oneself, with the outcome in one's own hands.
meaning.zh: 主动权掌握在自己手里。

examples.zh: 机会来不来不由我们，但努力与否操之在我。
examples.en: Whether chances come is out of our hands, but whether we try is up to us.

examples.zh: 谈判中我方操之在我，不必着急。
examples.en: In the negotiation the initiative is ours, so there is no rush.

usage.en: Often paired with 成败 or 主动权.
usage.zh: 常与“成败”“主动权”搭配。

meaning.en: A prosperous people and a rich state.
meaning.zh: 百姓殷实，国家富强。

examples.zh: 盛世之下，民殷国富。
examples.en: In a golden age, the people prosper and the state is rich.

examples.zh: 这位君主治国多年，民殷国富。
examples.en: After years of his rule the people were well off and the state wealthy.

usage.en: Formal; common in praise of good government.
usage.zh: 较正式，常用来称颂治世。

meaning.en: To live on in memory after death through great deeds or ideas.
meaning.zh: 人虽死去，功业或精神永远长存。

examples.zh: 英雄们死而不朽。
examples.en: The heroes are immortal in memory.

examples.zh: 他留下的作品使他死而不朽。
examples.en: The works he left made him live on after death.

usage.en: Often in eulogies and commemorations.
usage.zh: 常见于悼词与纪念文章。

meaning.en: To be silenced, unable or afraid to speak.
meaning.zh: 闭口不说话，形容不敢说或说不出。

equivalents: keep one's mouth shut out of fear

examples.zh: 在高压之下，人们钳口结舌，不敢议论。
examples.en: Under such pressure people kept their mouths shut and dared not discuss it.

examples.zh: 被问到账目，他顿时钳口结舌。
examples.en: Asked about the accounts, he suddenly clammed up.

usage.en: Literary; often describes silence imposed by fear or censorship.
usage.zh: 书面语，常指因恐惧或压制而不敢开口。

natural: clouds in the morning, rain at dusk

meaning.en: A poetic allusion to the union of lovers, from the legend of the goddess of Wu Mountain.
meaning.zh: 典出巫山神女的传说，诗文中借指男女欢会。

equivalents: a poetic image of a tryst

examples.zh: 词中朝云暮雨，写的是一段旧情。
examples.en: Clouds and rain in the lyric stand for an old romance.

examples.zh: 古诗里常见朝云暮雨的意象。
examples.en: The image of morning clouds and evening rain is common in old poems.

story.en: In Song Yu's rhapsody, the goddess of Wu Mountain tells King Huai of Chu: 'At dawn I am the morning cloud, at dusk the passing rain' (旦为朝云，暮为行雨).
story.zh: 宋玉《高唐赋》：“旦为朝云，暮为行雨，朝朝暮暮，阳台之下。”

date.en: late Warring States, c. 3rd c. BC

usage.en: Literary allusion; not for everyday speech and sometimes used in other senses such as changing weather.
usage.zh: 文学典故，不用于日常口语；有时也泛指变幻的天气。

pinyin: bó lā tú shì ài qíng

meaning.en: A purely spiritual love without a physical side.
meaning.zh: 纯精神层面、不涉及肉体的爱情。

examples.zh: 他们之间只有柏拉图式爱情。
examples.en: There was only Platonic love between them.

examples.zh: 她向往柏拉图式爱情，却难以在现实中实现。
examples.en: She longed for Platonic love, but found it hard to realise in real life.

usage.en: Borrowed from the Western term 'Platonic love' (coined from Plato's name); common in writing about romance.
usage.zh: 借自西方的“Platonic love”，常见于谈论爱情的文章。

natural: behind red gates, wine and meat go bad

meaning.en: The rich waste food while the poor starve: a line condemning social inequality.
meaning.zh: 富贵人家的酒肉吃不完而腐臭，而穷人却冻饿而死，批判贫富悬殊。

equivalents: the rich feast while the poor starve
a world of waste beside hunger

examples.zh: 看到食品浪费的数据，我想起“朱门酒肉臭，路有冻死骨”。
examples.en: Seeing the food-waste figures, I thought of the line 'wine and meat rot behind red gates while the frozen lie on the road'.

examples.zh: 贫富差距太大，难免让人感叹朱门酒肉臭。
examples.en: With such a wealth gap, it is hard not to sigh that the rich feast while the poor starve.

origin.source: 杜甫《自京赴奉先县咏怀五百字》

story.en: Du Fu, on his way home in winter 755, wrote: 'Behind the red gates wine and meat go bad; on the road lie the bones of the frozen' (朱门酒肉臭，路有冻死骨).
story.zh: 杜甫《自京赴奉先县咏怀五百字》：“朱门酒肉臭，路有冻死骨。”

usage.en: Usually quoted with the second half, 路有冻死骨. A sharp social criticism.
usage.zh: 多连同下句“路有冻死骨”引用，是尖锐的社会批评。

antonyms: 有田同耕，有饭同食，有衣同穿，有钱同使，无处不均匀，无人不饱暖
